The eye is visible, relatively large, and positioned laterally on the head, consistent with the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Separated dorsal fins; first dorsal spiny, second dorsal soft-rayed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish exhibits a single dorsal fin located far back on the body, near the tail. This is a definitive anatomical feature of the Pike family, whereas the barracouta has two separated dorsal fins further forward.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anal fin similar to second dorsal.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Due to the angle and the species mismatch, the anal fin structure does not match the barracouta description. It aligns with the posterior placement seen in pikes.
The caudal fin is forked, which matches the checkpoint description.
